div.head: Quadr II Praef 2
div.ab: Quod cum inclita bonitate regis et iure debita subditorum fidelitate proueniat, situs quoque patrie confidenter adiuuat, nature beneficiis et maris uicinitate conclusus, ut sine gratuita dominorum licencia nullus exitus, nulli relinquatur ingressus.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 542 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: And while this comes about through the renowned goodness of the king and the fealty of his subjects owed by right, the situation of the country also confidently aids it, enclosed by the benefits of nature and the nearness of the sea, so that without the free licence of the lords no exit, no entrance is left to anyone.
